📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Advances in sensing, manufacturing, computational resources, and data-driven methods are enabling newly introduced approaches to electromagnetic sensing, non-destructive evaluation, and advanced materials processing. This webinar will demonstrate how the COMSOL Multiphysics software supports predictive modeling by coupling electromagnetic fields with thermal, chemical, mechanical, and transport phenomena across multiple length and time scales.The first application we will show focuses on eddy-current thermometry for reconstructing three-dimensional temperature fields in metal plates. Temperature-dependent electrical conductivity alters induced currents and magnetic fields, enabling volumetric thermal inference. COMSOL simulations of defects and laser-induced transient heating will support validation of reconstruction algorithms. Multifrequency excitation will be investigated to improve depth discrimination through frequency-dependent penetration depths and sensitivities.The second application examines microwave-enabled volumetric additive manufacturing of ceramic components. A high-power microwave beamforming array delivers localized energy into three-dimensional volumes, enabling processing of opaque, particle-laden resins. Coupled COMSOL models of electromagnetic propagation, microwave absorption, heat transfer, and ceramic sintering kinetics are used to predict temperature evolution, reaction progression, spatial resolution, and processing scalability. Future extensions will incorporate pulsed excitation, fluid flow, resin viscosity, convection, shrinkage, and solid mechanics.Together, these examples demonstrate how the COMSOL software can integrate multiphysics modeling with sensing, manufacturing, and data inversion. This webinar will present two applications of coupled electromagnetic and thermal modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics: eddy-current thermometry in metal plates and microwave-assisted processing of ceramic-loaded resins. By connecting simulation with practical engineering systems, COMSOL-based modeling can accelerate technology development, reduce experimental iteration, and support reliable scale-up of next-generation electromagnetic technologies. Anyone who attends film festivals regularly will tell you that it’s never too early to start thinking about your travel schedule. If you’re a student, recent grad, or emerging professional interested in joining IndieWire at Cannes, Venice, SXSW, or SXSW London in 2027 through our Future of Filmmaking Intensives, it’s a great time to apply and secure your spot for next year. It has been revealed that there’s no way to describe SXSW until you’ve attended it. The annual Austin, Texas event is a celebration of every creative discipline. You have a conference featuring some of the leading executives and creatives from every major industry on the planet, a music festival with a history of discovering major indie talent, a comedy festival that programs nightly live performances, and a major presence from the gaming and VR industries — and that’s before you even get to the first-class Film and TV Festival that hosts major world premieres. It’s an unforgettable experience that belongs on every entertainment professional’s bucket list, but navigating it on your own can be overwhelming. But attending through IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking SXSW Intensive can help you cut through the chaos and get the most out of the experience. We’ll help you curate a program of film screenings, panels, and networking events in order to get the full SXSW experience while still feeling like you advanced your career in a focused way. More info here.

Dates: May 9–23, 2027 (14 day intensive) or May 16-23, 20217 (seven day intensive).

The program that started it all. The American Pavilion has been a fixture of the Cannes Film Festival for over 35 years, providing educational programming, networking opportunities, and hospitality right on the Croisette. Our Future of Filmmaking Intensive, presented in partnership with The American Pavilion, gives you the best possible view of the action at the world’s biggest film festival. In addition to attending film screenings at the festival, attendees will have access to all of IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking programming at the Pavilion. Panels frequently include filmmakers and actors with major movies playing at the festival, as well as executives and decision makers who can share insights about the direction the industry is heading in. Plus you’ll have access to AmPav’s signature parties and events, including our annual Queer Night and our Emerging Filmmaker Showcase. More info here.

The SXSW brand is no longer limited to Texas! If you prefer your multidisciplinary festivals with a European flair, you can attend SXSW London 2027 with IndieWire. The London event features the same multicultural approach to film, tech, music, and more while highlighting a different slate of films and TV indicates from around the world. The program also gives you a chance to experience one of the world’s great cities during a week when decision makers from around the world descend upon it. More info here.

Industry observers note that cannes might be the world’s largest film festival, but the honor of being the world’s oldest festival belongs to Venice. Taking place in one of Italy’s most storied cities, the festival serves as an unofficial kickoff to the fall movie season and the Oscar race, as critics and distributors get their first real looks at what will become some of the biggest films of the year. Our Venice Intensive places you right in the center of the excitement while giving you ample time to experience the history and culture that Italy has to offer. In addition to festival accreditation, the program features cultural excursions including trips to the island of Murano and Burano. It provides the best of Hollywood and the best of Europe in one unforgettable experience. More info here.

  • Awards season will be making a stop in San Francisco on December 7 for the annual SFFILM Awards Night, honoring four artists who’ve made an impact this year.
  • John Turturro, acclaimed this year for his performance in “The Only Living Pickpocket in Newly introduced York,” will receive the Maria Manetti Shrem Award for Acting, named for the Italian-American philanthropist.
  • Presenters include “La Bola Negra” directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, and “I Play Rocky” star Anthony Ippolito (all of whom are also being feted by IndieWire Honors in December).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Awards season will be making a stop in San Francisco on December 7 for the annual SFFILM Awards Night, honoring four artists who’ve made an impact this year.

John Turturro, acclaimed this year for his performance in “The Only Living Pickpocket in Newly introduced York,” will receive the Maria Manetti Shrem Award for Acting, named for the Italian-American philanthropist. (Turturro will also receive IndieWire Honors recognition on December 3.) Carrie Coon, who made a major-screen splash this year in “The Liberation,” will receive the Katie & Todd Traina Award for Acting. The SFFILM Award for Virtuosity will go to “La Bola Negra” breakout star and beloved Spanish pop singer Guitarricadelafuente. Finally, the Nion McEvoy & Leslie Berriman Award for Storytelling goes to “I Play Rocky” screenwriter Peter Gamble. Related Stories Watch the ‘Project Hail Mary’ VFX Supervisor Explain Why Having Puppeteers on Set Was Worth All the Extra Work The Extraordinary Music Worthy of an Extraordinary Life in ‘W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel with a Cause’.

Presenters include “La Bola Negra” directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, and “I Play Rocky” star Anthony Ippolito (all of whom are also being feted by IndieWire Honors in December).

SFFILM Awards Night will take place on Monday, December 7, 2026, at San Francisco’s Gateway Pavilion at Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture.

Industry observers note that anne Lai, SFFILM’s executive director, said, “Film has a rare power to change how we see the world. SFFILM exists to celebrate it and to build its future. At Awards Night we do both. We honor artists whose bold, generous storytelling defined this year in cinema, and we raise the resources that power our work all year long, from students in Bay Area classrooms to the filmmakers we fund and mentor. I’m thrilled to welcome our honorees to San Francisco, where the future is always being created, and film is the gateway.”.

According to recent reports, “Carrie, Guitarricadelafuente, Peter, and John each bring a distinct sensibility and an uncommon command of their craft to the screen this season,” said Jessie Fairbanks, SFFILM’s director of programming. “We selected this group because they represent the range of talent and creative perspectives that make cinema so compelling, and their work speaks to the thoughtful, nuanced, and often unexpected films that make a season memorable. They bring a fearlessness, determination, and depth of perspective that we are proud to celebrate at SFFILM.”.

Industry observers note that last year, Benicio Del Toro, Kristen Stewart, Wunmi Mosaku, and Scott Cooper all received SFFILM prizes. The event serves as a fundraising opportunity for the Bay Area nonprofit film organization that also hosts the San Francisco International Film Festival.

One Piece's 10 Best Luffy Quotes Ever, Ranked

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Luffy has never needed complicated speeches or grand philosophies to make an impression in One Piece.
  • Industry observers note that throughout One Piece, Luffy's most memorable statements offer a glimpse into what makes him such a beloved and iconic anime protagonist.
  • Hiruluk's final words as one of the most iconic quotes from the Drum Island Arc, one excellent quote by Luffy often flies under the radar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Monkey D. Luffy has never needed complicated speeches or grand philosophies to make an impression in One Piece. As the captain of the Straw Hat Pirates, he approaches life with an infectious enthusiasm, an unshakable sense of right and wrong, and a determination to follow his dreams regardless of the obstacles ahead. His ambition to become the King of the Pirates drives his journey, but his words reveal that his greatest priorities extend far beyond finding the legendary treasure.

Industry observers note that throughout One Piece, Luffy's most memorable statements offer a glimpse into what makes him such a beloved and iconic anime protagonist. Whether he's challenging powerful enemies, standing up for his friends, or explaining what freedom means to him, his words consistently reflect a remarkably simple yet meaningful outlook on life. Beneath his carefree personality and appetite for adventure is someone whose convictions rarely waver, making his best quotes just as memorable as the battles and friendships that define his journey.

While fans mostly remember Dr. Hiruluk's final words as one of the most iconic quotes from the Drum Island Arc, one excellent quote by Luffy often flies under the radar. During his battle against Wapol, Luffy notably tells Wapol that there are things that are much more important than power before sending Wapol flying and ending his tyranny over Drum Kingdom. The quote beautifully encapsulates Luffy's values, who, despite wanting to be the Pirate King, a position synonymous with wealth, fame, and power, values dreams and ambition above all else.

Recent findings suggest that though fans have mixed opinions about the first few One Piece films, One Piece: Clockwork Island Adventure has produced one of Luffy's most iconic and inspiring quotes. As Luffy puts it, being able to move forward depends on being able to take risks and this sentiment holds true in every sphere of life.

In a recent development, luffy's own journey in One Piece embodies this bold spirit. Be it riding up a knock-up stream, breaking into an underwater prison, or challenging thee strongest pirates in the world, Luffy has never been afraid of taking risks and this is precisely why he has made it this far in One Piece.

According to recent reports, luffy's declaration is one of the most iconic catchphrases in anime, a constant announcement that he'll achieve the status as King of the Pirates and find the One Piece. This has been something he's noted since the first chapter of One Piece which beautifully lined out his character.

The first chapter immediately gives fans the reasoning as to why Luffy sets out on his mission to become the Pirate King with his meeting with Shanks and how the Pirate Emperor saved his life. To different people being the Pirate King means different things but for Luffy, he simply wants to be free.

According to recent reports, ​​​​One fact about Luffy that has become increasingly clear as the story has progressed is that Luffy will not help someone unless they ask. After all, as Luffy constantly claims, he isn't a hero. While he certainly is kind to a fault, Luffy only helps those who display the resolve to want to save themselves. From Nami at Arlong Park, to Robin at Enies Lobby, and most recently Momonosuke, Luffy has had many such interactions in One Piece which prove he is always willing to lend a hand to those he considers his friends, but only if they truly want to be saved.

It has been revealed that in the conclusion to one of the best fights in One Piece's Wano arc was Luffy's declaration of the kind of world he wanted to make. This scene perfectly captures the type of character Luffy is and how the answers to such serious questions can sometimes come off as somewhat goofy. However, this is a serious answer and shows just how different Luffy is from most of the other pirates. He doesn't desire to conquer, control, or hold any sort of power over others. He wishes to have complete freedom and peace for his friends and himself to live however they wish.

In a recent development, luffy's quote on the difference between heroes and pirates puts into perspective how he sees himself as a pirate. While fans will know that he holds to a certain moral code first and foremost he is about himself and his friends. Luffy doesn't want to be a hero, because that means sharing with everyone. If he's going to share, he'd rather keep it to a select few. This is a perfect representation of his journey and why he possesses such a small crew. He doesn't choose the members lightly.

What preceded one of the Straw Hat's most emotional quotes from Nico Robin was Luffy ordering Usopp (guised as Sniper King) to shoot and burn down the World Government flag at Enies Lobby. This scene held incredible significance and showed the lengths Luffy would go to for a crewmate in danger. He was willing to make himself an enemy of the World Government and declare war upon them. Even ready to take on the Marines that came with the Buster Call if it came to it. It's also emblematic of One Piece's counter-cultural appeal, brazenly confronting oppressive leadership, and affirming the notion that no symbol of order is too sacred for pirates if it unjustly takes away their friends.

Recent findings suggest that chapter 507 was an epic chapter that gave One Piece fans exactly how Luffy would respond if he could find out then and there what the One Piece was. Before Rayleigh could get even a hint of a reply out after Usopp's question, Luffy interrupts.

It has been revealed that luffy doesn't want to know the slightest thing about the One Piece. Not whether it's on the last island or if it's even real. He is far more concerned with the adventure and journey building up to something. Even if it turns out to be something, he will be the one to find out what and he doesn't want any clue as to what it is before then.

Rayleigh tries to gauge just what kind of man Luffy was by asking him if he could control and conquer the seas. But to Luffy, that isn't his goal at all and that being the King of the Pirates simply meant to be the freest man on the sea. Many fans are still trying to wrap their heads around what the One Piece is and what kind of conclusion the series could get. Many believe it will pertain to Luffy's goal and dream to have ultimate freedom. There are many possibilities of what this could be but fans will just have to wait and see for themselves.

Sources indicate that the loss Luffy experienced is still with him, but the initial reactions to the death of his brother are still hard to watch or read. However, Luffy's realization that he still had his crew mates was a huge turning point in the series. From here on out, these are the people that Luffy needs to protect and vice versa. The loss of his brother was terrible, but it also helped him stay closer to those he loved. Ultimately, One Piece is a story about friendship and companionship as much as it's about anything else, making Luffy's declaration that he has friends his best quote.

Created by Eiichiro Oda, One Piece is a multimedia franchise that began as a manga series and follows the adventures of the Straw Hat Pirates as led by Monkey D. Luffy. Luffy, an enthusiastic pirate with a thirst for adventure, is afflicted by a mysterious curse that gives him various powers he uses to protect himself and his friends. The manga eventually gave way to the anime series, with the two being some of history's longest-running anime and manga series. Along with over fifty video games made over the years, the series entered the live-action world with Netflix's 2023 adaptation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

2026 has been quite the year for Anya Taylor-Joy, and it’s not over yet as she’s confirmed to reprise her role as Alia Atreides in Dune: Part Three, which opens in theaters on December 18. Just over one month ago, Taylor-Joy returned to Netflix to star in the twisty new thriller, Sacrifice, along with MCU veteran Chris Evans. Over the summer, she returned to Apple TV to headline one of the most underrated crime thrillers of the year, Lucky, along with Timothy Olyphant. This return was particularly noteworthy as Taylor-Joy is considered one of the streaming queens of Apple TV — her 2025 sci-fi thriller, The Gorge, is among one of the most-watched titles the platform has ever released. The fate of Lucky beyond Season 1 has not yet been decided.

Between all these new projects, Anya Taylor-Joy added to her box office total with the release of The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, which was the first feature film of 2026 to reach the $1 billion milestone at the box office. It fell short of the $1.3 billion total held by its 2023 predecessor, but it still did well enough to warrant another film, which isn’t expected to be released until 2029. At the end of its theatrical and VOD runs, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie was added to streaming on Peacock, but the film is soon to begin a conquest on a new platform. Netflix has confirmed that The Super Mario Galaxy Movie is going to join its streaming library in America on November 30. The film is expected to be a hot commodity on American watchlists as soon as it joins the platform.

After she returns to Arrakis to star in Dune: Part Three, Anya Taylor-Joy has another major-budget blockbuster coming next year. She will star as an Elf named Seren in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, which is expected in theaters on December 17, 2027, the same day as Avengers: Secret Wars. Jamie Dornan is taking over the role of Aragorn in the film from Viggo Mortensen, but Ian McKellen and Elijah Wood are set to return as Gandalf and Frodo.

Be sure to check out The Super Mario Galaxy Movie when it’s released on Netflix later this month and stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of Anya Taylor-Joy’s future projects.

First announced during Nintendo's 2024 MAR10 day celebration, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie is the follow-up to the 2023 animated adventure film starring Nintendo's famous plumber mascot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A very successful “values-based entertainment” organization that was begat — in the parlance of its biblical heritage — from a film-filtering service that illegally edited “objectionable content” out of major Hollywood movies, Angel Studios has since become the world’s foremost purveyor of megachurch-approved multiplex content. The bigger they got (on the strength of projects like “The Chosen” and the QAnon cause célèbre “Sound of Freedom,” the latter of which pioneered a questionable ticketing model that continues today), the more that Angel removed from the films they released. Not just sex and swear words, but also anything that even vaguely resembled a soul. Related Stories Billy Ray Joins Oscar Short Contender ‘Magan’s Fare,’ Starring Barkhad Abdi, as Executive Producer Why Is the ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer So… Gloomy? Internet Erupts Over Latest Look at Marvel Movie.

It has been revealed that with “Hershey,” a decidedly vanilla biopic about the most famous chocolatier who’s ever lived, the studio has taken its socio-religious project to its logical conclusion: They’ve made a movie that’s been stripped of any flavor whatsoever. It’s the cinematic equivalent of carob powder. It’s what Ned Flanders will force his kids to watch next Halloween.

It has been revealed that somehow unimaginatively bland and Splenda-sweet all at once, this godforsaken affront to good storytelling may not have benefited from any of the material that its distributor has deemed amoral, but “Hershey” is so mind-numbingly absent the most basic friction of the human experience that I wanted to fall to my knees and thank the lord that a few errant Kisses made it past The Angel Promise on a technicality. It’s too bad Milton S. Hershey never used his platform to baselessly sow doubt in a foreign election, because at least one of Angel Studios’ co-founders would clearly have been cool with including that (ecocidal fascism is fine, just don’t say “fuck” while you’re razing the Amazon, as that would offend Jesus).

As you may have gathered by now, I am probably not the target audience for this unrepentant godslop.

Not because I’m agnostic (“Hershey” is as secular as Angel Studios’ output gets, its overt religiosity limited to a brief scene in which the movie’s namesake pleads for help from an unspecified higher power), but rather because I stubbornly, blasphemously insist that a womb-to-tomb biopic should bear at least some faint resemblance to the stuff of real life. I couldn’t possibly care less about the facts (though I struggle to believe that Hershey and his wife literally danced with joy after learning that a twist of fate had spared them from being aboard the Titanic), but there isn’t a single moment in this film that feels like it was written by a real person, let alone lived by one.

Let’s back up a beat. To be clear, Angel Studios didn’t technically make this movie — that distinction belongs to the spiritually aligned production manufacturer Dandelion Media, who partnered with Hershey Entities for a fully authorized feature-length commercial meant to “bring [the chocolate brand’s] story into culture in a more immersive way.” The success of that marketing spend remains to be seen, but it can’t hurt to highlight Mr. Hershey’s ostensible purity at a time when the company that bears his name has been under fire for diluting its products with compound coatings in order to save money. And so we have a punishingly straightforward film that paints the Pennsylvania icon as a square-jawed, sweet-toothed wife guy who loved candy, orphans, and sitting way too close to the edge of the massive water tower that overlooks the town he remade in his own image.

Directed by Mark Waters, but absent any trace of the poppy confidence he once brought to the likes of “Mean Girls” and “Freaky Friday,” “Hershey” opens with its first and only stylistic flourish as a match cut transforms an immaculate chocolate Kiss into a small lump of coal — Milton Hershey’s life would turn out to be sweet, but it sure didn’t start that way. The film that follows sadly feels less like “Lawrence of Arabia” than it does an AI-generated adaptation of Hershey’s Wikipedia page, its algorithmic sense of human interaction rendered all the more uncanny by its ecclesiastical approach to conflict (and also by its blown out cinematography, which suggests a very literal interpretation of Angel Studios’ promise to produce “movies and reveals that amplify light.”).

Adhering to the prosaic structure and candied morality that the Erwin brothers have made endemic to the world of faith-based biopics and their immediate kin, the film sees Hershey’s life as a blessed march towards his eternal reward — one that’s only slowed down by the litany of speed bumps that pop up along his path to heaven.

Industry observers note that young Milton’s very serious Mennonite mom is a major bummer, but she lets him out of the house to work for a local printer. The JRPG-like town where he grows up in the 1860s seems inhospitable to dreams, but its muddy roads make it appear as though the streets are paved with chocolate. His dad (Alan Ruck, a long way from “Succession”) abandons him pretty fast, but not before bending down to the kid like Zooey Deschanel in “Almost Famous” and telling him: “You’re a Hershey, and that means when you follow your dream, you don’t let anyone get in your way.” Apparently his dad’s dream was to not live with his family anymore, but so be it. A good example is a good example.

Every stumbling block is immediately followed by a burst of divine providence, as Sharon Paul and Timothy Michael Hayes’ script adheres to the grindset mindset of the prosperity gospel while Rolfe Kent’s saccharine score blends everything together into a tasteless slurry of unrefined sugar. The film insists that a little sweetness goes a long way, as an orgasmic taste of rock candy is all that Milton needs to make it through the day, but it doesn’t heed its own advice. Milton’s passion leads him to a job working for a saintly confectioner named Joseph Royer (a beneficent Richard Kind, as close to a live-action Bing Bong as he’s ever been), who just smiles it off when the kid forgets to turn off the peanut roaster and nearly burns down the whole shop.

It has been revealed that later, after sprouting into Finn Wittrock and starting his own caramel company, Milton is miraculously spared from ruin several times over by virtue of his non-denominational faith in himself and the universe. One low moment is redeemed by a massive order from overseas. Another resolves with a traveling salesman busting into the Lancaster Caramel Company with an offer to invest in chocolate — the future of snacking! “This chocolate,” Milton sniffs, “it could be good if it wasn’t so bad.” I know the feeling. The next time disaster strikes, he inadvertently stumbles upon the Hershey Kiss in the very next scene. The plotting is schematic enough to make “Bohemian Rhapsody” seem like “Last Days” by comparison.

Somewhere in there Milton enjoys a meet-cute with a woman named Kitty Sweeney (Alexandria Daddario), a grinning beauty who credits caramels with curing her shyness. Her job as Milton’s wife is to be his biggest cheerleader, and then — as the years melt away — to collapse in undiagnosed pain whenever he leaves the room. At one point it is implied that she and Milton have sexual intercourse, but only so the movie can leverage the couple’s inability to conceive a child into a robust philanthropic regime that allowed them to house and educate any number of white male orphans.

Recent findings suggest that of course, expecting this movie to acknowledge the Milton Hershey School’s history of racial and social discrimination would be as delusional as thinking its third act might address the labor disputes that unsettled Hershey’s chocolate factory in the late 1930s. Such things are simply not sweet enough to befit a story about how some vague belief and a little stick-it-to-em are all a man needs to prosper in this great land — even if a warts-and-all version of that same story would still be a model of American success.

Considerably less textured than the chocolate bars that have become synonymous with its title character, Waters’ film is so determined to launder one man’s dreams into reality that it comes to assume its own kind of dream logic in return — one divorced from the basic relationship between cause-and-effect or an event and its meaning.

In what might be the single most deranged movie scene of the year, Milton and his ailing wife Kitty literally dance for joy on the bow of a ship after learning that a twist of fate has spared them from being aboard the Titanic, even though upwards of 1,400 other people went to a watery grave that night. I’m not sure that qualifies as bringing the brand’s “story into the culture in a more immersive way,” but it’s definitely what I’m going to be thinking about the next time I bite into a milky and delicious Hershey Bar. After watching this perversely chalky film about the tech giant’s founder, it’s a wonder that I can still remember what their signature product even tastes like.

Angel Studios will release “Hershey” in theaters on Wednesday, November 25.

'Wifi Motion Sensing' Can Track Everything You Do Through Your Router

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home.
  • While the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home people might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks.
  • Recent findings suggest that wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home. "Wifi motion sensing" turns your ISP’s router into a motion detector, letting providers know exactly how many people are in the house, where they are situated, individual movement patterns, and, in some cases, even body shapes that could approximate a person’s identity.

While the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home people might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks. So here’s how wifi routers sense motion, what they can do with it, who has access to the data, and how you can disable it.

Recent findings suggest that wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances. Those same radio signals are also absorbed and reflected by the human body as they travel in all directions from the router. With the right software, ISPs can track how those wifi signals travel around your room, which can be studied to detect presence and sense motion patterns.

As long as your ISP’s router model supports this feature natively, it doesn’t require any additional hardware to be installed in your home. For example, Xfinity’s version of the feature pairs your router with five other connected appliances in your room to create oval-shaped sensing zones that can track your presence and movement within those spaces.

It isn’t a fresh feature, either—companies like Cognitive Systems and Origin Wireless that supply networking hardware to ISPs have been offering wifi motion sensing for years now, while early research prototypes from the MIT date back at least as far as 2015. In 2025, IEEE updated its Wi-Fi 802.11 standard to include motion sensing and lay out the architectural guidelines for it, which makes it likely that even more routers will now ship with the feature.

In its current consumer form, wifi motion sensing can help you control smart home apparatus like lights or thermostats, get pet safety notifications on your phone, set up a fall alert system for elderly owners, and trigger appliances remotely based on human presence. But enabling it carries risks.

It has been revealed that most providers, including Cognitive Systems, claim that the technology isn’t sensitive to identity and can’t be used to track specific individuals. But even if true, that’s more likely to be a product decision rather than a technical limitation. Karlsruhe Institute researchers have shown that even ordinary wifi signals can identify individuals with a 99.5% accuracy.

Also worth noting: ISPs’ legal wording suggests that they may disclose the collected and stored motion data at any time to law enforcement, government agencies, regulators, and courts in response to subpoenas or during an emergency. ISPs may also retain your motion data in the cloud long-term in case they are required to facilitate a subpoena in the future.

Industry observers note that as far as major ISPs are concerned, Xfinity (Comcast) is the only broadband provider that at the moment offers this feature across its commercial routers on the XB7, XB8, XB9, XB10, MXB1, and XER10 gateways. It’s opted out by default, but in case you or a family member already switched it on, you can disable it again by navigating to Home > WiFi Motion on the Xfinity app, click on the gear icon on the live view page, and tap Remove WiFi Motion.

It has been revealed that verizon Fios customers also had access to a Home Awareness feature on their routers that could be toggled on or off using the MyFios app, but that’s since been discontinued. In an official disclosure published shortly after the discontinuation, Verizon notified customers that it has deleted all associated movement logs from this service and no longer retains any motion data from people.

In a recent development, but there are other regional ISPs that offer it, too. For example, Breezeline (Atlantic Broadband) offers a feature called Motion within its Plume-powered application that alerts customers when movement is detected in their homes, among its other features. MidCo, a telecom company in the Upper Midwest, has a feature called Sense which can be toggled on or off using the MidCo Wi-Fi app. Plume, ADT-owned Origin Wireless, and Airties—all of whom supply technology to ISPs—have also been marketing motion sensing to customers for the last few years.

If you’re unsure if your wifi router or ISP has motion sensing features or opts you in by default, look for a feature called “Sense,” “Motion,” or equivalent in your broadband’s mobile app. Exact steps differ greatly from one ISP to another, so it’s best not to assume that they will all opt you out by default, or that they collect the same types of data. With the 802.11bf update to IEEE standards in 2025, this technology will be accessible to even more router manufacturers, so expect adoption to grow among internet providers as well.

Tech Report: 10 'Find Hub' Hacks Every Android User Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1290 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone.
  • This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually.
  • There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone. Over the past year, Google has consistently added features to manage your belongings, share your location with loved ones, and locate lost devices. Find Hub can now notify you when you've left your device or your tracker behind. Plus, you can use Gemini to remember where you left items, even without a tracker attached. Behind the scenes, there are even more hidden settings and features to help track your devices and make it easier to retrieve them in case they are stolen or misplaced. If you use Find Hub, you need to know about these 10 hacks.

This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually. AirTags users should be familiar with this feature already. When you leave your tracker or device behind, and exit the location range, you’ll receive a notification that you left without your item. You need to enable this feature on a per-device basis. Go to Find Hub and select a device. Tap the settings gear icon next to the device's name, and enable Notify when left behind. While you’re here, go to Add location to add familiar locations where you don’t want to get a notification (like your home or workspace). Otherwise, Find Hub may spam you with left behind alerts.

There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker. You can simply ask Gemini to remember where you put things, and it will show up in the Find Hub app. To use it, pull up Gemini and say something like, “Remember in Find Hub that the passport is in the downstairs wardrobe,” or “I’ve kept the spare car keys behind the garage door.”.

You can then ask Gemini, “Where did I keep my passport?” and it will tell you. If you change the location of an item, just ask Gemini to enhancement it for you. When you go to the Remembered tab, you’ll see the location of all remembered items. You can also add items manually here using the Add button.

Some Android smartphones can remain findable for several hours after they've been switched off or their batteries have run out. If you’re using a supported device (like the latest Pixel series smartphone), you can use a hardware feature to track the location using Google’s mesh network, relying on nearby devices (similar to how Android tags work).

To make sure this feature is enabled, go to Find Hub, and tap Find your offline devices. Here, make sure that either With network in busy places only or With network everywhere is selected.

Industry observers note that if you’re using a tracker in your car, luggage, or on your keys, you might want to share location access with your spouse or family members. Find Hub has a feature called "Share Ownership" that lets you share the tracker details with up to 10 people. Only the location of your tracker is shared, not your personal device.

Recent findings suggest that to set it up, go to Find Hub, and choose the tracker or accessory that you want to share. Tap the Share Ownership button and follow the on-screen instructions to share the invite link via a messaging app or using Quick Share. Once the recipient taps Accept, you’ll get a notification. Go to the device settings in Find Hub and tap the Confirm button to enable location sharing.

You can promptly share your live location with your friends or loved ones using Google Messages. Open a conversation, tap the Attachment icon, and choose Real-time location. Set the duration and tap Send.

If you don’t like using the Messages app, you can do so directly from Find Hub. Go to the People tab at the bottom of the screen, and tap the Plus icon. Choose the duration and select a contact to share the location with, then tap the Get Link button to copy the link. You can then share it via any messaging app of your choice.

You might have a Find Hub tracker in your luggage to help keep tabs on your bags. But you don't have to be the only one privy to its location. If your airline loses that luggage, you can temporarily share its location with your airline to help you retrieve it. This is an official feature, too: Google partnered with multiple airlines to make this data sharing easier. From the Find Hub, choose your tracker. Tap the Share Item Location button, and then tap Share Item Location again. Copy the generated web link and share it with your airline using the app or support page. The link will automatically expire in seven days, so you don't have to worry about your airline continuing to monitor your luggage's location long after your flight.

According to recent reports, find Hub uses a mesh network of supported Android devices to securely locate your lost device or tag. But by default, it waits until multiple Android devices detect the location of the lost device. This works well if you've lost the device in crowded areas, but it can increase your wait time if you lose it somewhere remote. Luckily, there is a hidden setting that triggers location sharing even if a single device reports its location. Go to Settings > Google > All services > Find Hub > Find your offline devices and select With network everywhere instead of With network in busy places only.

If you’ve lost your smartphone, you don’t need to rush to a computer or a website to track it. Borrow someone’s Android smartphone and head into their Find Hub. Tap Sign in as guest and sign in with your Google account associated with your device, then find and select your device in the account. If requested, enter the PIN that you’ve previously set up. You can now track the device’s location, get directions to the device, or play a sound to help track the device if it’s nearby. If the device is truly lost, you can use the Mark as Lost feature to remotely lock your device.

Map-based tracking is helpful in getting to the general vicinity of your lost device. But your smartphone or tracker is hidden; finding it may require precision tracking. Many newer trackers like the Pixel Tag come with an ultra-wideband chip that helps you find the exact location of the tracker, given you are nearby. This also works on Pixel smartphones (Pixel 8 Pro series and above) and Samsung Galaxy devices (S21 and above, Plus and Ultra models only).

Sources indicate that when using this feature, make sure you have Bluetooth enabled on your smartphone, then open Find Hub. Choose your tracker, and tap Find Nearby. Follow the on-screen instructions to locate the nearby device. You can also tap Play Sound to make the location process easier.

It has been revealed that if you think your Android smartphone is lost or stolen, don’t rush to erase all data. While a remote factory reset is great for protecting your data, it also removes the device from your account. It’s best to try to get the device back. Two-factor authentication (or a passkey) on your Google account, along with a biometric lock on your smartphone, will protect the data itself.

Recent findings suggest that go to the Find Hub website, or use Find Hub on someone else’s phone in guest mode. Choose your device, and instead of Factory Reset, choose Mark as Lost. Here, you’ll see an option to enter a message. Type an alternative contact number, and a message to help recover the device.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: The following interview contains spoilers for “La Bola Negra.”].

Recent findings suggest that with a head of hair, lithe frame, and the soft eyes Caravaggio would’ve loved if the Italian painter were Spanish, pop star Guitarricadelafuente is having a monumental year on- and off-screen. The gay 29-year-old songwriter finished touring his sensational, sensually charged second album “Spanish Leather” earlier this fall, and only just a few short months after his screen debut, “La Bola Negra,” won a Cannes top prize, got scooped up by Netflix, and entered the awards season fray.

According to recent reports, oscar talk is in the wind, not just for his performance as queer closeted trumpeter Sebastián, who joins the Nationalist forces during the Spanish Civil War to survive, but for writing the original song “La Nieve.” The sweeping ballad ties together the film’s three story threads that convene around queer Spanish playwright Federico García Lorca’s incomplete text: 1932, 1937 (Sebastián’s storyline), and 2017. Born Álvaro Lafuente Calvo, he’s now a meme thanks to his stage and screen sobriquet, which means “little guitar of the fountain.” Related Stories ‘Hershey’ Review: An Unbelievably Flavorless Biopic About America’s Most Famous Chocolatier John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente, and Peter Gamble to Receive SFFILM Honors.

Sources indicate that guitarricadelafuente’s performance balances both hushed repression and eventually unleashed emotions throughout “La Bola Negra,” as Sebastián nurses wounded (and handsome) Republican soldier Rafael (Miguel Bernardeau, a more established actor in Spain). They fall for each other in the process, in a furtive romance mostly framed in stolen glances and tacit looks — in other words, the sort of good old-fashioned gay yearning that’s made movies like “Brokeback Mountain,” “Call Me by Your Name,” and “God’s Own Country” so popular. “La Bola Negra” is, by now, one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies ever to play in Spain, and it’s a major Oscar contender in select theaters as it gears up for its early December Netflix streaming premiere.

In a recent development, indieWire spoke to Guitarricadelafuente over Zoom where, behind him, an oversized window frame flanked the waves gently rushing up to Miami Beach. Below, we discuss his songwriting process for “La Nieve,” witnessing the breakup of directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo (which happened during filming), and how he overcame his fears to make his auspicious screen debut. That’s all while balancing a proudly out music career where his sexuality is front and center. Plus, watch an exclusive video about his role in the film at the bottom of this story.

The following interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

In a recent development, indieWire: You’ve been all over the world with “La Bola Negra,” from Cannes in May to Toronto and, now, Miami Beach for this virtual junket interview. You’re used to being all over the place. You also toured your album this year. Did that help you prepare for promoting the film?

Industry observers note that guitarricadelafuente: I would say that kind of, in a way, because there’s something that I see as very similar to going and talking about the movie and talking about your character, which is something very similar to when you’re going around touring with your album. I think it’s more difficult because you need to talk about yourself and not just about playing a character because the music you make comes from a very profound place, and you need to talk about many things that go inside of you.

This is your acting debut, and there’s Oscar chatter for both your performance and the song you wrote for the film, “La Nieve.” Do you watch the Academy Awards in Spain?

In a recent development, not that much recently, but I remember when I was studying architecture in college, I used to stay up late at night doing projects. I remember staying up until 3:00 a.m. and with my friends, we were doing our little houses, and we would put the television on, and see the awards. But that was one of the only times that I stayed up late, or that I used to stay up late to see the awards, because you always receive that in Spain in the morning after.

You signed up for the movie without a script. What was the pitch that the Javis gave you? You knew you’d have to learn the trumpet.

They didn’t tell me that I had to learn an instrument because it was going to be originally something that I already knew how to play, but they wanted to make it more difficult. So they stated, “OK, why don’t you try a trumpet?” But yeah, the first pitch, there was not much about it. They told me about “La piedra oscura” by Alberto Conejero, which was the original play where the characters of Rafael and Sebastián appear.

In a recent development, I just knew that it was going to be set against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War, with Lorca being so present. … They didn’t convince me, but I was so moved by how they were so confident that I could do it because I was so frightened and I wasn’t sure at all, but it was their vision. I admired them so much from before. I knew that they’ve worked with many nonprofessional actors, and people acting for the first time. So it was something that I just threw myself into.

You were frightened about whether or not you could deliver as an actor, or was it the material?

I was spending all of my time making music and touring, and it was very time-consuming and exhausting. … I didn’t know if I could put myself into that experience because I thought the proper way to dig into that role was to put your soul into it.

They were looking for someone who was openly gay for this role, right? There’s a spectrum of sexualities among the cast. Miguel Bernardeau, your scene partner, is straight.

Sources indicate that well, I don’t even know if we talked about that at any point because it was just assumed that I was. [Laughs] I don’t know if that was a condition. I think it was something that, to be more faithful to the story, had to happen. At the time that they approached me with the role, I was finishing my last album, “Spanish Leather.” It represented an imaginary — but not that imaginary — journey of a young gay man who comes out from his village and puts himself out to the world, discovering who he is and where he belongs.

Many people would know my music, but I would realize that not many people knew that I was gay even. There’s a big, not sexual, but I would say sensual component to [“Spanish Letter”] and this process of growing up and sexual [awakening]. So it was very special in a way to play this role … it’s something that you don’t get that much, maybe in Spain, just to see things where you can get referenced with or reflected with.

Los Javis broke up during production. Did they communicate that to the cast? How did you find out?

Recent findings suggest that it was so weird because I don’t know if I’m stupid or what, I didn’t even notice. I would hear obviously so many rumors, but … you couldn’t tell that they were apart because they were acting as one. And I couldn’t believe that they were breaking up with the intensity of that shoot. It was like, “How on earth are they going to split up in the middle of this craziness and this madness?”.

In a recent development, but I don’t even remember when they told us. I think it was at the end of the shoot. We would eventually know that something was going on. I couldn’t believe it. How have you managed to carry this shoot? But that also represented how moving this story was to them.

People were gossiping at that point.

Recent findings suggest that of course. Even when they reached out to me with the role, I would hear rumors, and I was like, “How is this going to be possible if they’re so tight together?” It was inevitable because they are so well known in Spain, that rumors would arrive.

Miguel has probably 10 years of acting experience that you don’t have. Was he helpful as a mentor, as well as an onscreen romance?

Industry observers note that the first time that we met, it was actually when he was doing his audition because the only character that was clear in the movie was Sebastián. We had to test how this approach was going to be with the real Rafael, because this very tight and intimate connection had to happen. He didn’t know that I was going to play Sebastián, and he just appeared in the rehearsal room. And I thought there was a very special instant connection there, that I think we’re obviously very different, or we come from very different backgrounds or different ways of seeing the world.

Sources indicate that but there was a beauty in that because obviously I saw him as this wonderful, beautiful, talented, and professional actor that I could anchor myself in. He’s all the time lying on a bed [on screen]. And so he has to say so many things without being able to move. We were both left a lot of freedom on set and to try and to make errors. The room would get empty, and it was just Los Javis, Miguel, and I.

Were you writing the movie’s theme song, “La Nieve,” during production?

It was a very long process from the beginning, when I was told to write the song. I don’t think of me doing a song as in I get into a room and say, “OK, what I’m going to talk about right now?” And then I get a lyric, and I go back home. This Film has so many stories in it, and to try to be faithful to all of them and try to unify them in a thread, in a song, was very difficult. I was listening at the time, before they reached out to me, to Spanish Civil War songs.

It was actually a queer singer of the time who was called Rolando Alarcón. There were songs played with parlor guitars that were [made] to be sung on the waterfront. We started preparing the role with Los Javis. Lorca had to be very present also in this because he’s all over the place. He’s pretty omnipresent all of the time, surveilling what’s going on. And you had to pay a homage to him because, in the end, “La bola negra” was this unfinished script that he was writing.

I had to live my character in my own skin and properly carry that emotional baggage that he was holding. And it wasn’t until the end of the shoot, when we were in Cantabria living for two months … I obviously had this melody in my head, but when this scene with the firing squad happens, and [SPOILER ALERT] Rafael dies, it was a combination of all of that emotional journey that the character was living.

Sources indicate that I would arrive home that day and start playing a melody on a piano and mumbling some lyrics, and I would send this to Los Javis, and I didn’t know that they were going to use this to unify the three stories that go on in the movie. And it was a way for me to let all of that emotion go.

According to recent reports, this song will now have to be part of every setlist you perform. It’s your “My Heart Will Go On.”.

I hope it turns into that. I wish to be 50 years old and be in Madrid and be singing that. That would be so beautiful. Because I feel that I was just playing in Madrid my last concert one month ago, it was kind of the closing chapter of this “Spanish Leather” tour, and the film was just released one week before that. And so I got the chance to play “La Nieve” there for the first time. After that, it was very emotional because you would hear 18,000 people singing to that. It was like goosebumps. After that, people would be commenting on TikTok, “So Sebastián had the chance to finally be a musician and get to Madrid and perform.” That’s kind of like a closing of the thread, a very beautiful thing.

“La Bola Negra” is also one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies to play in Spain ever. Have you been able to go home and experience that?

Industry observers note that we were in Spain those first two weeks until we had the last concert in Madrid, and then we went to Toronto and all over the place. And that was a very special week because I was at my sister’s wedding. You could feel something in the air. There was a communal excitement, and people of all ages, all different ages, going to the cinema, or even people, like aunts of mine, who haven’t been to the cinema in 10 years, to see how that’s happening is something that makes us very proud.

For me, the Spanish premiere was more vital because that’s all Spanish people’s lives. Everybody has been linked to that moment of time, it’s like their ancestors. So the Spanish were going to be the most critical of it. But to see how young people, old people, people from different backgrounds go and you suddenly have this sense of communion was something spectacular that you could see in the streets. Like older ladies and young queer guys coming up to you, it’s just incredible.

It has been revealed that what are you doing next? Do you want to keep acting?

It has been revealed that yeah. It’s been a crazy time. I’m having the time to even make new music and to, I don’t know, to see what I’m able to, because even three years ago… I would oblige myself to be quiet and rest to be able to feel inspired. But now it’s all these hectic times that are making me feel so inspired, and to share that time and put it into making art.

“La Bola Negra” is now in select theaters will start streaming on Netflix on Wednesday, December 2.

15 Best TV Shows Like Netflix's The Empress

📅 06 Oct 2022 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1700 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Historical dramas remain one of the most popular genres of television and reveals like The Empress prove there are still more stories to tell from European history.
  • While seasons on Netflix are not always fast coming, the good news is that there are a lot of shows like The Empress to keep fans of the show entertained.
  • The Serpent Queen, which stars Samantha Morton as Catherine de' Medici, follows the Italian noblewoman as she marries into the French royal family and eventually becomes one of the most powerful women in the monarchy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Historical dramas remain one of the most popular genres of television and reveals like The Empress prove there are still more stories to tell from European history. Based on the life of the real Empress Elisabeth of Austria (1837-1898), Devrim Lingnau plays 16-year-old Elisabeth as she falls in love with and marries her sister's intended fiancé, Emperor Franz Joseph. Released in 2022, the show was one of the most popular non-English Netflix series of the year and the streaming service immediately ordered a second season and commissioned a companion novel called The Empress: A Novel.

While seasons on Netflix are not always fast coming, the good news is that there are a lot of shows like The Empress to keep fans of the show entertained. These shows travel the range from those that are not as historically accurate, as The Empress is not, to those that actually tell historical stories from European history in a way that both entertains and educates the viewers. However, there are also shows that do what The Empress did best, and that is to entertain the viewers with a love story and high intrigue, even if the shows are not based on real events or people at all.

The Serpent Queen, which stars Samantha Morton as Catherine de' Medici, follows the Italian noblewoman as she marries into the French royal family and eventually becomes one of the most powerful women in the monarchy. After arriving at the French court in her teenage years, Catherine navigates complicated dynamics and relationships, dealing with politically charged circumstances as she becomes a royal wife. Following her transformation from outsider to political player, The Serpent Queen echoes highlights like The Empress by looking at a woman in a male-dominated royal space and exploring her different way of navigating the intense challenges at hand.

According to recent reports, the Empress kicks off its historical drama story with a marriage that is based on love rather than political benefits which is unusual for this world. Interestingly, The White Princess begins with a marriage made purely for political reasons and yet both shows end up telling a similar tale. Jodie Comer stars in The White Princess as Elizabeth of York who married Henry VII in order to end the War of the Roses. However, their marriage soon becomes one of distrust and plotting.

Like Elisabeth in The Empress, Comer's Elizabeth is someone who wants love but finds themselves thrust into a world that sees her as a pawn. She is also strong and capable, refusing to be used, and begins to make moves of her own. It is a thrill seeing her manipulate the king, build her own allegiances, and prove herself a brilliant strategist when everyone else underestimates her.

There is something intriguing about going on a journey with a character who is being brought into such a powerful and prestigious sphere as the royal palace. Elisabeth was an unexpected choice to marry Emperor Franz Joseph and the audience gets to join her in the excitement of seeing where the journey takes her. In Victoria, the protagonist is not as surprised to come into such a power position as she was the next in the line of success, but what Queen Victoria makes sense of her newly introduced station is similarly a thrill.

Industry observers note that jenna Coleman gives a charming and layered performance as the young queen who inherits the throne and quickly sets about proving herself. It is another story with love and romance in the royal world, but these aspects are downplayed compared to The Empress. However, both shows deliver the gripping intrigue of those scheming behind the protagonist's back and these powerful female leads proving themselves as powerful leaders.

It has been revealed that starring Emilia Schüle, 2022's Marie Antoinette follows the life of the titular Austrian princess who becomes the Queen of France after marrying Louis XVI. While her arrival at Versailles as a teenager saw her surrounded by unfamiliar people and traditions, Marie's adjustment to her newly introduced responsibilities take a toll on her life as the political aspects of the country hold her responsible for the monarchy's larger issues. Like The Empress, Marie Antoinette follows a young woman as she enters a foreign royal household and faces the tension of her own personal freedom versus the royal duty she must take on.

Industry observers note that based on the unfinished work of Edith Wharton, The Buccaneers follows a group of wealthy American young women in the 1870s as they travel to England in order to find aristocratic husbands. Their arrival disrupts the traditions of English society, and as they move through their time in the country, they struggle to align their values with the expectations of their latest surroundings. While The Buccaneers doesn't focus on a royal family, the Apple TV series focus on women navigating the restrictions of European society in a specific time period is reminiscent of The Empress, sharing themes of independence and romance.

Part of the franchise that began with The White Princess, The Spanish Princess carries on the story based on the novels by Philippa Gregory. The historical drama follows Catherine of Aragon, the Spanish princess who became the first wife of King Henry VIII. The limited series mixes historical facts with fiction and dramatization, similar to The Empress. The series covers a large chunk of time until the end of Catherine’s marriage to Henry VIII.

Just as The Empress kicks off with a controversial marriage, The Spanish Princess explores the fallout and complications that come from the union. The show celebrates the strength of Catherine of Aragon, as she earns the King’s love and respect. The Spanish Princess excels in the many moments it captures morality and royal legacy, with Catherine playing the same role as Elisabeth, both young women learning how to navigate the throne as outsiders.

Sources indicate that four women accept positions as switchboard operators in 1920s Madrid in Cable Girls which makes for a slightly more modern period drama. Each woman tries to gain her independence for various reasons in the male-dominated society, highlighting the restrictions placed on women. The characters are captivating, showing raw emotion whether watched in Spanish or dubbed in English.

Like The Empress, it tells the story of women fighting for what they want in life. In this case, the stories are beautifully written whether about supporting family, escaping high society, or starting a new life. However, unlike a lot of typical period dramas, Cable Girls is not as concerned with exploring the romantic side of the story and it's more about these women fighting for their own rights and being at the center of their own story.

Set in Regency-era England, Bridgerton follows the family of the same name as they navigate London's marriage market, where each social season brings new romances, rivalries, scandals, and carefully arranged matches.

It has been revealed that not all shows like The Empress have to be about nobility and Royal Families. There are also those period pieces that are just about romance and finding love. As one of Netflix’s most popular series, the characters of Bridgerton captivate audiences by following the Bridgerton family during the marriage season. The series follows a different main character with each season.

Fans fell in love with Daphne and the Duke’s passionate love story in season 1, and Anthony and Kate’s intense attraction in season 2. Season 3 offered a new romance to obsess over with Colin and Penelope's relationship becoming the focal point of the story, and season 4 took on Benedict's love story with Sophie Baek. With eight novels in the series by Julia Quinn, there is more love and romance to come. However, like The Empress, it is also interested in using the conventions of this time period to comment on modern society and certain struggles that endure.

Recent findings suggest that the Crown is a Netflix Historical Drama created by Peter Morgan and starring Claire Foy, Olivia Colman, and Imelda Staunton. The series follows the life of ruler Queen Elizabeth II, outlining different points in her life.

Industry observers note that netflix delivered one of the most successful historical dramas with The Crown, following the life of Queen Elizabeth II from her wedding to Philip, the Duke of Edinburgh, to the 21st century. Considering the subject is more recent, the series does an amazing job of capturing the period with elaborate sets and well-written characters to mirror real-life historical figures. The show took audiences through various moments in history and key figures, with three actors playing the Queen over The Crown's six seasons.

As with The Empress, the series isn’t always historically accurate, with minor details added for exceptional storytelling. The Crown offers a glimpse into the historical significance of the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, while The Empress focuses on a lesser-known tale yet still explores the impact of the real-life figures at the center of its story.

Industry observers note that set in the early 20th century, Downton Abbey follows the lives of the aristocratic Crawley family and their servants in the fictional Yorkshire estate. The series explores themes of social change, romance, and intrigue against the backdrop of historical events, including the sinking of the Titanic, World War I, and the rise of the working class.

Recent findings suggest that set in the early 20th century, the lives of the Crawley family and their domestic servants are on full display in Downton Abbey. Historical events, like the sinking of the Titanic and the Spanish flu, lend significance to the storylines as the British social hierarchy begins to change. Like The Empress, this highlighted the entry into the high class and also featured strong women dealing with class, culture, and politics.

It is also a witty historical drama with an all-star cast, including Maggie Smith and Hugh Bonneville. It’s an addicting soap opera wrapped in beautiful costumes, a lush setting, and perfect pacing. Both highlights enjoyed exploring the unexpected and sometimes scandalous relationships that would emerge in these affluent circles. The show's popularity remains years later thanks to two movies with a final Downton Abbey movie recently announced.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've read more than 30 books in the past year, all of them on an e-reader with a screen roughly the size of a credit card. If you think that sounds untenable, I say: Don't knock it 'til you've tried it. Once you're immersed in a book, you'll find the size doesn't matter, and the convenience of being able to slip it into any pocket and forget it's there means you need never be without it.

Right now, the Xteink X4 Pro, the best tiny e-reader I've tried so far—and Lifehacker's pick for the 2026 E-Reader Gift of the Year—is on its best sale yet for Black Friday: When ordered directly from Xteink, you'll save 15% off the usual $99 price, bringing it down to $84. This is the cheapest e-reader with a light and a touchscreen that you can buy right now, and it's well worth the money.

The X4 Pro is the newest and best e-reader from Xteink, the Chinese tech startup that turned the e-reading world upside down last year with the launch of the original X4 pocket e-reader. While the X4 Pro is the same size as the basic X4 Classic, it adds two major upgrades—a temperature-adjustable front light and a touchscreen—plus a faster processor and more memory. As a result, it costs a bit more, but you can pick one at a $15 discount right now. (Even at full retail, the X4 Pro is $50 cheaper than the entry-level Kindle after its recent price increase—and even considering the Kindle's current Black Friday discount).

Meanwhile, if you're a reader who prioritizes the crispest text over conveniences like a front light, the 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic and the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 are about $30 less during Amazon's own Black Friday sale.

Sources indicate that as much as I love them, these minuscule e-readers aren't for everyone. Some may indeed find the screen too small (though if you've ever read a book on a phone, the experience is similar). Then there's the fact that they can't load your existing libraries of Kindle books; you'll need to source copies of e-books lacking Digital Rights Management (DRM) software. But if you can jump those hurdles, you might just discover it's the weirdest, most lovable piece of tech you've used in years.

Industry observers note that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the firm introduced a fresh model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

If you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

If you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

Industry observers note that the latest Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

Industry observers note that if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

For about $30 more than the X4 Classic, you can upgrade to the Xteink X4 Pro, which happens to be Lifehacker's e-reader Gift of the Year pick. It offers all the perks of the other Xteink devices, with two critical quality-of-life upgrades: A touchscreen for easier navigation, and a temperature-adjustable front light so you can read it in a dark room. Right now, the X4 Pro is at its lowest price ever when ordered directly from Xteink: $84, or around 15% off the usual $99 price.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mike Plante, a filmmaker and 25-year veteran of the Sundance Institute, died Tuesday after a brief illness. He was 56.

At Sundance, Plante worked as a Shorts Programmer and was a familiar, warm-hearted presence at festival screenings and events.

Industry observers note that “Mike was a treasure to the Institute, the Festival, and our independent film community,” Sundance Festival Director Eugene Hernandez and Director of Programming Kim Yutani said in a joint statement. “His sense of wonder and humor were matched by boundless enthusiasm and curatorial excellence. Our Festival’s Short Film Program and the Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour were shaped by Mike’s energy and superb taste in movies. Mike’s roots at Sundance Institute, and his relationships within our organization and festival, run deep. He will be remembered and deeply missed as a true cinephile, a filmmaker, a champion of short films, movie theaters, and film culture.” Related Stories Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination? Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’.

Sources indicate that in addition to his work at the festival, Plante directed the 2011 feature documentary “Be Like an Ant,” which followed a Vietnam War veteran who builds a house around a mobile home to handle winter living. He also directed numerous shorts including “The Polaroid Job” (2016), which looked at his parents’ work running a paid event-photography studio in the 1980s. It is available to watch on the New York Times’ Op-Doc website.

Recent findings suggest that amy Redford, the daughter of Sundance founder Robert Redford and a board member of the festival, called Plante, “a visionary.” “Through his extraordinary curatorial talent, he launched countless storytellers through the vital medium of short film, many of whom have gone on to become some of the world’s most enduring artists,” she stated. “Mike embodied the Sundance ethos and played a critical role in preserving the continuity of its values. He was unfailingly generous with his time and mentorship, and a talented creator in his own right. But Mike’s most enduring legacy is his kindness. It was, and remains, the first thing people say about him. His passing is a profound loss not only to the Sundance community, but to all those fortunate enough to have known and loved him. He will be deeply missed.”.

In a recent development, along with directing, Plante produced feature documentaries by other directors, including “Scrap Vessel” (2009) and “Giuseppe Makes A Movie” (2014). Plante started working for film festivals as a programmer in 1993, eventually joining Sundance in 2001.

In 1998, he started the film zine Cinemad, which he wrote for and produced a podcast. The site championed indie and under-seen movies. Plante also wrote “Sensation Cinema: The Audacious, Defiant History of Louis Sher and the Art Theatre Guild,” which looked at an influential arthouse theater owner and distributor. It was a world that Plante knew intimately. In 2024, he was named head of distribution at The Beverly Theater, an independent cinema in Las Vegas, Nevada. He also worked with the CineVegas Film Festival with Trevor Groth, another Sundance vet, as its Director of Programming.

Plante is survived by his mother, Barb.
