  • Our grandparents could drop some treats in a sock and call it Christmas, secure in the knowledge that their children would be delighted by an orange.
  • In a recent development, I don't know anyone who wouldn't appreciate finding these display glasses in their Christmas stocking.
  • It can be hard to buy a gift for a health-focused person.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our grandparents could drop some treats in a sock and call it Christmas, secure in the knowledge that their children would be delighted by an orange. These days, though, everyone from your tech-obsessed granny to your cutting-edge teen wants to be impressed. Luckily, there's a mind-blowing high-tech gadget out there for everyone.

In a recent development, I don't know anyone who wouldn't appreciate finding these display glasses in their Christmas stocking. The Xbx a01s are sunglasses you can plug into any device with a USB-C port to create your own personal, private monitor. The resulting picture is the equivalent of a 142" TV. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz, and the glasses support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling and billions of colors, all in a package that weighs only 62 grams. In other words: It's an HD TV you can carry in your pocket and wear on your face. The $299 list price won't break your wallet either. They're the best smart glasses for most people. Check out my full review for more details.

It can be hard to buy a gift for a health-focused person. They usually don't want booze and they like putting in effort. But the Whoop Peak 5 fitness tracker will brighten the Christmas morning of the most diehard athlete. It's more versatile than a watch (you can wear it on your bicep and even in your underwear) and it monitors heart rate, respiratory rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, blood oxygen levels, daily activity, and sleep—basically everything I don't worry about. Check out Lifehacker's senior health editor Beth Skwarecki's in-depth look at the Whoop Peak 5 for more details.

Recent findings suggest that you cannot go wrong with a GoPro. The company's easy-to-use, hard-to-break cameras are synonymous with "action photography" and compact enough to fit in a stocking. If there's a snowboarder, skateboarder, kayaker, or BMX racer on your list, this is a must. Even if your giftee isn't an adventurer, the GoPro Hero 13 supports additional lenses and filters that let people go beyond the "gnarly fish-eye, dude" photography and videography of past generations. Check out associate tech editor Michelle Ehrhardt's GoPro Hero 13 review for more details.

Everyone wants their own droid. Beni from Mondo Robotics is a camera robot that takes 4K video while autonomously following its subject wherever they go. If you want to get action footage, there's no need to hassle with a tripod or another person: You can control Beni with the remote, or simply tell it to follow you. It can be set to track you from behind, from the side, or it can circle you, and you can adjust what it is doing from the app or remote on the fly, so there's no limit to the kind of elaborate shots it can pull off. Plus it's freakin' adorable. The $799 list price might be a bit steep for most gift-givers, but as far as how well it works and how much fun I've had using it, it's worth the money.

Industry observers note that the R36 Max 2 retro handheld game console lets you take your gaming anywhere. It comes with over 20,000 games pre-installed, so you can play every title from classic consoles like the Atari 2600 or the PlayStation 1, as well as just about every arcade game anyone ever dropped a coin into, all for less than $100. I paid more than that in quarters just to beat Dragon's Lair!

Industry observers note that I'm obsessed with the Yamaha Seqtrak. It crams a drum machine, sequencer, sampler, three separate synthesizers, and a speaker into a package small enough to put into a Christmas stocking. It's a complete mobile studio—everything you need to produce a song or beat—but it also integrates with your computer's DAW and other MIDI gear to become part of your home studio. All that for only $300!

Sources indicate that the Flipper Zero is a must-have device for the hardcore, glasses-wearing, circuit-bender type of techie. Its ability to do evil deeds like hack ATMs is greatly exaggerated, but the Flipper is still a technological Swiss Army knife that lets you read and manipulate the invisible waves around you, from radio waves to RFID, NFC, Bluetooth, and wifi signals. It's educational, fascinating, and powerful; how you use that power is your business.

According to recent reports, if you're giving a gift to a would-be Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, this miniature, wireless microscope will rock their holiday. It's easy to set up, works with PCs, Android, or iOS devices, magnifies things up to 1000x, and takes 1080p pictures of your discoveries.

10 Hacks Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1243 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far.
  • I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are key.
  • If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far. The world feels even more detailed and immersive than previous GTA games, which means there's a lot to learn beyond the basic tutorials and prompts the game shares at the beginning. These are the 10 GTA 6 hacks I used to improve the game's quality of life. If you do the same, you'll spend more time immersed in the world, and less time fighting the game's default settings.

I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are key. If you ignore all the optional quests or small asks by other characters, you won't be able to return to those later. These are small things like fixing up the house for Lucia, meditating with her, and buying her a necklace when she asks you to. All of these have an impact on your progress. Take your time in this chapter, and remember to save before starting the mission called "Recalibration." That mission leads to Tourist Trap, which is the point of no return for Chapter 1.

If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different. It's hard to keep an eye on minimap directions while you're also getting used to vehicles in the game, and I used voice navigation to ensure that I don't keep getting lost, particularly for time-sensitive missions. You can enable this by going to GTA VI settings > Audio > GPS Voice > Voice. If you're playing the game on PS5, your DualSense controller's speaker plays GPS voice prompts. This is great as those alerts can be hard to hear over all other in-game sounds from your TV's speaker.

Using GTA 6's default controls, making Jason and Lucia run is quite annoying. The game makes you hold L3 to run, which hurts my thumbs. If you alter movement speed in settings, you can make the characters run just by using the left stick. You can walk by easing off the left stick, or switch to a fast walk, jog, or run when you push the stick all the way. Tweak this by going to GTA VI settings > Gameplay > Movement Speed > Jog. This lets you move faster without draining your stamina. You can also change from Jog to Run if you want the fastest possible movement speed with the left stick. Having stated that, my pro tip is to go to Control Scheme in settings, and switch to Classic. This lets you run by holding the X button, as opposed to L3 with default controls.

Haptic strength is one area where GTA 6 takes the immersion a bit too far, as it's dialed up to the maximum level by default. This makes the controller's vibration strength a bit too intense for my liking, and also has a negative impact on battery life. You can fix that by reducing haptic strength a little. It's under GTA VI settings > Controller > Vibration & Haptics Strength.

Many modern controllers develop "stick drift," an concern where small movements of the analog sticks register as large inputs. This causes a major problem in games that require precise inputs, such as GTA 6. To counter this potential problem, the game allows you to adjust the deadzone for each analog stick in your controller. That stated, this setting can be used to your advantage, even if you don't have stick drift complications in your controller. I recommend dialing up the deadzone to 7 to improve the driving experience. I find most cars in GTA 6 to be a bit floaty to drive, and adjusting the deadzone fixes this issue to a large extent.

According to recent reports, committing a heist attracts heat in GTA 6, and there are many different ways to escape the attention of in-game cops. The usual tricks include stocking up on outfits to change into, parking your vehicle a block or two away, and being so stealthy that you leave no witnesses to your crimes. However, an underrated trick involves using the pickup truck you get at the start of the game. Get a bike in the game, and stash it in your pickup truck. Then, use the truck to drive to the crime scene, and hide the truck a short distance away. Unload the bike, and use it to get to the crime scene. Once the heist is complete, ditch the bike, and run to your truck. Witnesses won't have seen you using the truck, which allows you to escape the area quickly.

Sources indicate that if you are using a car as a getaway vehicle, you can use two tricks to make a smooth escape. First, double-tap the Triangle button to exit your vehicle without switching off its engine. When you return to the vehicle in a hurry, you can escape a lot faster. If you have quick fingers, you can double-tap Triangle first, and just as your character is about to exit the vehicle, press L3 (or X, if you use classic controls). This leaves the car's door open, and saves you a little more time when you're fleeing.

In a recent development, I suffer from chronic migraines, and I am sensitive to bright lights. Fortunately, GTA 6 has a bunch of accessibility settings that help me play the game for longer. Even if you don't face the same issues, these settings will help reduce eye strain in longer play sessions. Go to GTA VI settings > Display > Flashbang, and switch to Dark. This stops flashbangs from showing a bright white light when they go off. On the same settings page, you can tweak Player Status Effects Intensity to reduce screen effects when your character is low on health or stamina. You can also enable Brightness Reduction to reduce the intensity of bright lights in the game, and try Focus Trail Colorblind Mode if you find it hard to distinguish between different colors.

Industry observers note that I haven't been able to play first-person shooters for decades because the camera movement makes me nauseous and gives me a headache. Of late, I've noticed that it's getting harder to play third-person games too. My first two hours in GTA 6 had me quite worried because I was feeling quite sick, and I had to turn off my PS5. Luckily for me, I found a few tweaks to mitigate this problem. You can do that in GTA VI settings > UI > Persistent Center Dot. This permanently shows a white dot in the center of the screen, and it reduced my motion sickness enough to help me play the game. You can also go to GTA VI settings > Camera, reduce Camera Bob, and turn off Camera Shake, and Weapon Sway. I also recommend going to the Controller tab in settings, and tweaking all the options under Aim & Look Sensitivity until you find a comfortable level.

GTA 6 includes realistic ringing sounds that linger after explosions in the game. This may be fine for some people, but it can negatively affect some players' gaming sessions. Those who suffer from tinnitus or chronic migraines may not enjoy those ringing sounds, and, luckily, the game allows you to disable them. Open GTA 6's in-game settings, and enable the feature from Audio > Tinnitus Reduction.

#188652. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • In a recent development, last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

In a recent development, last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Sources indicate that the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully rolled out on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

In a recent development, “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” notes Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

Industry observers note that more than 10 years in the making, MMX debuted on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a latest rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

It has been revealed that if all goes according to strategy, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to proposal, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” notes Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

Sources indicate that the best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

According to recent reports, “It will bounce probably several times,” indicates Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

According to recent reports, A simulation reveals how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

In a recent development, the WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she claims. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

It has been revealed that the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday states.

Industry observers note that despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Idefix’s interactions with its newly introduced home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec indicates. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel indicates the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel indicates. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Industry observers note that probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu indicates.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

Industry observers note that that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

According to recent reports, once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

It has been revealed that finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

In a recent development, “We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel notes. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (951 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that at today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the tech giant introduced two newly introduced frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks.
  • Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model reveals 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.
  • Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that at today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the tech giant introduced two newly introduced frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model reveals 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

In a recent development, microsoft indicates MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

Industry observers note that this doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

It’s also important to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft showed slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these upcoming models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex.

Industry observers note that one thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the firm paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the firm’s vast product line.

In a recent development, if you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As users adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous.

There’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

This becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft confirmed MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the tech giant itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Recent findings suggest that let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a company is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these upcoming models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first.

It has been revealed that A tech giant with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

According to recent reports, A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

It has been revealed that there’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Microsoft claims the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the new models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open issue.

The company also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these upcoming models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

According to recent reports, erielle Sudario is a Collider News and Feature Author from Australia and has worked in the journalism industry since 2018. When she's not writing, you can see Erielle building keyboards, reading a good book, playing video games, and creating content on social media.

It has been revealed that with only a month until Jumanji's fourth and final film, Jumanji: Open World hits theaters, fans will have the chance to immerse themselves in its adventurous world. A brand-upcoming VR experience has been announced, letting players face challenges, bond with exotic animals, and solve puzzles as the "fate of Jumanji" falls into their hands. If you want to know what it's like to be Dr. Bravestone, this would be your chance.

Industry observers note that the Jumanji film series began in 1995 and was based on the 1981 children's picture book by Chris Van Allsburg. The movie stars Robin Williams, Kirsten Dunst, David Alan Grier, and Bonnie Hunt, and the story follows two kids who play a magic board game whose effects spill into real life, like animals and hunters appearing in their world. In 2017, the board game returned, this time transformed into a video game, where a latest generation of players were sucked in and had to complete it to get home.

Now, free-roam VR entertainment firm Zero Latency has announced a brand-fresh game coming out this December called Jumanji: The Lost Levels. According to a press release, the company worked closely with Sony Pictures to create an original story that ensures that it "captures the wild, funny and chaotic Jumanji energy." This is what the game's description has to say:.

"Players will navigate the perils of Jumanji across a series of escalating challenges: forge bonds with exotic animal companions, survive an exhilarating river rafting gauntlet, bust out their best moves in a snake dance-off (yes, really), crack the secrets of ancient temple puzzles, saddle up and ride dinosaurs through uncharted jungle, and face off against an epic boss battle with the fate of Jumanji itself hanging in the balance.".

Recent findings suggest that the trailer for the upcoming game shows players controlling the same avatars seen in the movie as they explore the jungle and dangerous locations that thrust them straight into the adventure. Zero Latency first started in 2013, and since then, it has expanded worldwide, with over 30 locations in the U.S. alone, with six more venues opening soon.

Sources indicate that jumanji: Open World is the fifth installment and final entry in the Jumanji franchise. The movie takes place immediately after the events of Jumanji: The Next Level, as the world of Jumanji breaks free from its video game console and enters the real world. The video game avatars of Dr. Smolder Bravestone (Dwayne Johnson), Professor Sheldon Oberon (Jack Black), Franklin Finbar (Kevin Hart), and Ruby Roundhouse (Karen Gillan) roam the real world in "demo mode." It's now up to Spencer Gilpin (Alex Wolff) to set things right, and joining him in the game are his mother, Janice (Marin Hinkle), kitchen worker Donatas (Dan Hildebrand), and Tyson Shepherd (Jack Jewkes).

Jumanji: Open World will enter theaters on December 25, 2026, while Zero Latency's Jumanji: The Lost Levels will be released worldwide on December 4, 2026. Follow Collider for more updates.

Industry News: 10 Most Universally Loved Power Rangers Seasons, Ranked

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2306 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Power Rangers has always been defined by reinvention.
  • Still, even among the best Power Rangers shows, there’s only a handful whose quality seems beyond debating.
  • Sources indicate that saving civilians feels like the central purpose of Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue, and that clarity gives the season enormous appeal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Power Rangers has always been defined by reinvention. Across more than 30 years, the franchise has introduced dozens of Ranger teams, regularly swapping familiar faces, powers, and villains while still staying true to its ever-endearing central concept. However, every upcoming incarnation was a risk. Some became instant favorites, while others leave fans counting the episodes until the next team arrives. Fortunately, Power Rangers has produced considerably more hits than misses, with its strongest indicates demonstrating just how much variety the core idea of a team of Zord-piloting heroes in colorful suits can accommodate.

Still, even among the best Power Rangers shows, there’s only a handful whose quality seems beyond debating. These are the seasons that regularly unite fans who otherwise disagree about almost everything. They’re the Power Rangers series that manage to capture everything there is to love about the franchise with almost no criticisms from anywhere within the fandom. They represent a wide variety of eras and central gimmicks, but all of them manage to tap into the essence of what makes Power Rangers fans fall in love with the Rangers and their three-decade-plus battle against evil.

Sources indicate that saving civilians feels like the central purpose of Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue, and that clarity gives the season enormous appeal. Airing in 2000 during the original Saban era, it follows adults recruited to defend Mariner Bay from demons using powers developed through human technology. Firefighter Carter Grayson (Sean Cw Johnson) embodies the appeal. Helping people was already his purpose long before a Morpher entered the picture and he became the Lightspeed Rescue Red Ranger.

The emergency services gimmick makes the Rangers feel like essential members of their community, with responsibilities that extend beyond defeating monsters. Rescue vehicles, an underwater headquarters, and organized support staff give the heroes a convincing working environment, while it remains undeniably a Power Rangers story thanks to demons bringing danger their technology can’t always deal with. Plus, Ryan Mitchell (Rhett Fisher), the Titanium Ranger, adds an endearing redemption story and an original Ranger identity created specifically for the American series. It’s a satisfying blend of professionalism and supernatural adventure that few other Power Rangers shows can match.

There is an infectious enthusiasm to Power Rangers Dino Charge that makes it almost feel like a love-letter to everything that came before. Its dinosaur powers, colorful alien threats, and expanding Ranger lineup turn the search for the Energems into a lively and gripping adventure. Beginning on Nickelodeon in 2015 under Saban and continuing with Power Rangers Dino Super Charge in 2016, Dino Charge brought a welcome dose of energy and enthusiasm to the franchise. The team feels genuinely enthusastic about being Rangers, and that excitement gives viewers plenty of reasons to follow their adventures.

The unusual backgrounds of the Rangers in Dino Charge makes it especially endearing compared to many other Power Rangers demonstrates. Koda (Yoshi Sudarso) is a prehistoric human adjusting to modern life, while Ivan (Davi Santos) brings a medieval knight’s sense of honor into the group. At its core, Dino Charge is beloved because it has a team of Rangers fans are just as happy to spend time with out of costume as they are watching battle. That character-focused approach gives its increasingly elaborate adventures a human center, turning what could have been yet another dinosaur season into a team adventure with a particularly generous supply of personality.

Recent findings suggest that few Ranger teams are as immediately comfortable in their own company as the central trio in Power Rangers Ninja Storm. Shane Clarke (Pua Magasiva), Tori Hanson (Sally Martin), and Dustin Brooks (Glenn McMillan) have an easygoing and authentic chemistry that makes their friendship convincing before their training produces dependable heroes. When their ninja academy is attacked, the three students find themselvs as its unlikely defenders. Their mistakes are part of the attraction, giving their eventual competence a satisfying foundation in shared experience and growing trust.

In a recent development, the 2003 Power Rangers season launched the franchise’s New Zealand production era under Disney with a noticeably playful identity. Extreme sports, elemental ninja abilities, and enthusiastic comedy give it a distinctive flavor. However, it knows when to get serious too, with arcs like the emergence of the Thunder Rangers complicating the team’s playful dynamic. That balance of breezy entertainment and meaningful progression ensures Ninja Storm continues to be considered a highpoint by the Power Rangers fandom.

Terra Venture gives the Power Rangers Lost Galaxy team something unusually tangible to protect: an entire traveling community attempting to build a future among the stars. The 1999 Saban season combines its science fiction premise with ancient swords and living animal Zords, creating a distinct identity that, decades later, feels like one of the best representations of what makes Power Rangers’ style of storytelling so unique. However, that’s not the greatest creative achievement of Lost Galaxy. The core of why this Power Rangers series endures is that its Rangers share their journey with the inhabitants of Terra Venture, for whom danger is an ever-present aspect of daily life.

Every major setback threatens something much bigger than the outcome of the next battle, and the colony’s vulnerability gives the Rangers’ responsibilities a deep emotional grounding. What’s more, Lost Galaxy doesn’t hold back from exploring some of the darker implications of its dangerous premise. Kendrix Morgan (Valerie Vernon) sacrifices herself to save others, while Leo Corbett (Danny Slavin) grows into his leadership role through a series of incredibly difficult decisions. Meanwhile, central villain Trakeena (Amy Miller) was among the most ruthless villains Power Rangers had seen up to that point. Few shows in the franchise explored what heroism actually demands like Lost Galaxy, and it deserves every bit of love the fandom still has for it.

The 2009 season immediately stood out because humanity had already lost most of the world when Power Rangers RPM begins. Survivors shelter in Corinth while the computer virus Venjix (Andrew Laing) controls the wasteland outside, giving the Rangers an unusually desperate assignment. The Rangers aren’t here to save the world, they’re here to protect what little remains of it. The final newly introduced season of Disney’s ownership, RPM builds an absorbing story around the people carrying that burden. Doctor K (Olivia Tennet) is especially memorable: her incredibly well-written, guarded behavior born of a painful history gives the team’s technical expert a depth beyond creating upgrades.

According to recent reports, of course, Power Rangers isn’t Power Rangers if it’s incredibly bleak, and it's impressive how confidently RPM manages to retain a sense of light-hearted adventure and the franchise’s token comedy despite the setting being one of darkest the show’s ever seen. The friendship and interpersonal drama of the Rangers helps Power Rangers RPM keep the atmosphere of the wider franchise without losing its own unique identity. The combination of the season’s ruined world with its exceptionally well-written characters and its masterful tonal balancing act secured RPM’s place as a Power Rangers show fans have been returning to time and time again for over a decade and a half.

According to recent reports, teamwork is at the heart of the appeal of Power Rangers, but every fan knows that this aspect works best when it's earned after the Rangers have to overcome personal differences. Few seasons pulled this off as well as Power Rangers S.P.D., whose Rangers Jack Landors (Brandon Jay McLaren) and Sky Tate (Chris Violette) gave the franchise one of its most satisfying friction-laden story arcs. One arrives with natural leadership instincts and an unconventional background, the other believes his discipline and training should put him in command. Their struggle to respect one another counts for some of the franchise’s best character drama, with the S.P.D. team having to learn to become an effective unit by reconsidering their individual ideas of what a leader should be.

It has been revealed that this interpersonal tension works even better thanks to S.P.D. having one of the most distinctive Power Rangers settings. Released in 2005 and set in 2025, S.P.D. imagines humans and aliens sharing Earth, with Space Patrol Delta defending them from criminal threats and invasion while supported by an entertaining ensemble of characters like Commander Anubis Cruger (John Tui). Its futuristic world is enjoyable on its own, but the team’s gradual growth makes spending time there rewarding for reasons beyond the unique sci-fi trappings.

It has been revealed that bringing Tommy Oliver (Jason David Frank) back as a mentor figure was an inspired way to connect Power Rangers Dino Thunder with the franchise’s beginnings. The 2004 Disney season didn’t just feature Tommy as a nostalgia-grabbing cameo, either. His experience as a veteran Ranger was necessary to guide three very different students as they discover dinosaur powers and learn to become the Morphin Grid’s next generation of heroes. His presence made the world of Power Rangers feel continuous in ways it hadn’t for years, with the younger Rangers ensuring the energy and sense of adventure at the core of the franchise remained intact.

Recent findings suggest that dino Thunder also boasts some of the most satisfying character arcs of any Power Rangers season before or since. For example, Trent Fernandez-Mercer (Jeffrey Parazzo) has a White Ranger storyline that masterfully ties into Tommy’s own history. Meanwhile, central villain Mesogog (Latham Gaines) gives Dino Thunder’s take on the already-done dinosaur theme a sinister edge that distinguishes it from previous prehistorically-rooted Ranger stories. The result has both the accessibility of a fresh beginning and the satisfaction of an established universe. It gave longtime viewers meaningful continuity while introducing a Ranger team worth following in their own right, a feat few versions of Power Rangers have managed.

No Power Rangers show rests on the shoulders of a single character, but it’s impossible to ignore how much Pink Ranger Jen Scotts (Erin Cahill) gives Power Rangers Time Force an exceptionally strong emotional center. Her determination, grief, and gradual acceptance of the burden of authority make her one of the franchise’s most compelling leadership figures. What’s more, her developing relationship with Wes Collins (Jason Faunt) gives the season a romance with genuine dramatic weight that’s rarely seen in the franchise. The 2001 Saban series sends officers from the year 3000 into the present to pursue escaped mutant criminals. That premise may seem straightforward, but Time Force uses it as a foundation for some deeply emotional storytelling.

Jen, Wes, and the other Time Force Rangers regularly find themselves having to decide whether the futures laid out for them are worth protecting from change, and what changing those futures might cost the people they love. This underlying existential tension is supported by some of the most well-written and rounded characters in Power Rangers history. Eric Myers (Daniel Southworth) brings resentment and class tension to his rivalry with Wes, while Ransik (Vernon Wells) makes prejudice a central theme of Time Force’s villain arc. Understanding his anger never means excusing what he does with it, but it’s much more satisfying than an antagonist whose goal is taking over the world for no discernible reason beyond wanting to conquer it.

Sources indicate that while it aired almost 30 years ago, the two-part finale of Power Rangers in Space, “Countdown to Destruction,” was a game-changing moment for the franchise. Power Rangers had flirted with serialized narratives in its earlier seasons, but in Space finally unlocked their full potential. Released in 1998 during the original Saban era, it sends the Rangers beyond Earth to search for their captured mentor and confront an expanding alliance of villains. The cosmic scale was unlike anything there’d been in the franchise up until that point. Not only did the show manage to pull off this huge shift in scope, but it managed to do so with a level of success that even future space-based Power Rangers seasons haven’t really matched.

Power Rangers in Space pulled off something spectacular by making the franchise’s interconnected universe feel emotionally coherent. The villains like Astronema (Melody Perkins) and The Psycho Rangers remain fan-favorites too, both because of their aesthetic and because of how genuinely threatening they felt compared to the foes prior versions of the Rangers had faced. The true masterstroke, though, was that Power Rangers in Space never lost sight of the people at the heart of the story no matter how vast the adventure grew. That combination gives its conclusion an exceptional impact that still resonates with fans today. Years of colorful adventure culminated in choices and sacrifices that still define Power Rangers at its best.

Industry observers note that it feels almost cliché to say that the first Power Rangers season remains its most beloved, but that doesn’t make it any less true. The franchise may have grown considerably since Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, but many fans still consider it the apex of everything that keeps them committed to the Rangers and their adventures. Launching in 1993, MMPR turned teenagers, martial arts, dinosaur machines, and gloriously theatrical monsters into an irresistible identity. Its original team made heroism feel inseparable from friendship and a shared desire to do good.

That wholesome energy remains central to the franchise’s appeal years later, and nowhere does it feel purer and less distilled than in the Mighty Morphin era. The martial arts action is intense, the Zords make the moments that teamwork culminates in victory feel spectacular, and the Rangers’ civilian lives in Angel Grove make it feel like a home worth defending. However, the story had a lot of emotional depth to it too, especially during arcs like Tommy Oliver’s journey from Rita Repulsa’s evil Green Ranger to becoming the White Ranger and leading the team. Power Rangers has always been built on the idea that ordinary people can become extraordinary when they work together, and no iteration feels like it delivers on this enduring ideal quite like MMPR.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

Why Black Friday Is the Perfect Time to Start a Gym Membership

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most people are probably waiting until Jan.
  • The week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit.
  • This week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a upcoming air fryer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the new year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

The week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on upcoming tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

This week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a upcoming air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:.

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for newly introduced Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

Deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:.

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

It has been revealed that try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

According to recent reports, be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

According to recent reports, gyms also run sales around Newly introduced Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

That's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're newly introduced. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

Industry observers note that from Black Friday to Upcoming Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K plan works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your Fresh Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

Recent findings suggest that this is also the season when many workplaces and health intends wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:.

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some intends include gym memberships or discounts.

In a recent development, HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before New Year's resolution time arrives.

It has been revealed that the Rings of Power took a while to find its feet, but each season has improved on the last. The show had a monumental task ahead, further expanding J.R.R. Tolkien's high fantasy masterpiece without using material from his other works. Tolkien's estate has only permitted adaptations of The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit, so The Rings of Power has used the books' appendices to go deep into the history of Middle Earth and explore a character who is central to both movie trilogies, but despite shaping the fate of the world, is never truly seen.

In a recent development, people who have only seen Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings movie trilogy saw Sauron briefly in armor but mostly know him as The Great Eye, watching from the tower of Barad-dûr and communicating in the language of Mordor. However, while he is briefly mentioned in The Hobbit book as "the Necromancer," the movies expanded on this role. Now, The Rings of Power is showcasing this ability. Seeing Sauron's journey from master craftsman to The Dark Lord onscreen is, at last, winning audiences over, with The Rings of Power's third season getting its highest Rotten Tomatoes audience score yet.

Industry observers note that sauron's stealth introduction as Halbrand was an unusual decision that instantly added intrigue to The Rings of Power, but it was not necessarily popular with fans. The Lord of the Rings is one of the greatest high fantasy stories ever written, and is told through character studies and an epic scale rather than a mystery box format. Still, the show appeared to learn from this initially polarizing setup and explore Sauron as a character with motivations and skills in the second season, which revealed his extraordinary talent as a blacksmith.

The three seasons of The Rings of Power.

Rotten Tomatoes critics' rating.

Rotten Tomatoes audience rating.

In a recent development, as we know that The Rings of Power will eventually cover how Sauron created The One Ring, setting up this ability through his blacksmithing now feels like his backstory is being filled out, instead of being told through confusing exposition. Sauron's motivations and desire to shape the world according to his will are explored through this creative talent, and the way his skills parallel his view of the world act as much better character building. This is now paying off, with season 3 revealing the much more sinister magic that we know he has.

Sauron's shocking necromancy scene in which he reveals the truth about Theo's father gives viewers a glimpse of his potential. Not only does he appear to act as a messenger for Theo's dead father, Fäldred, but he uses the information he is given to manipulate Theo into taking one of the Rings of Power. The question of Theo's eventual identity is still being debated, but it is possible that we have just seen Sauron create the Witch-king of Angmar. With his dark magic scenes bringing his talents for creation and corruption together, Sauron is now entering a upcoming phase.

Industry observers note that sauron goes through several names in Tolkien's Middle Earth saga, and while it is not possible to put an exact year on The Rings of Power due to time jumps and compressing Tolkien's histories, season 3 takes place in the middle of the Second Age, with the character honing his manipulation skills. However, his dominant set of talents in the third season foreshadow his Third Age name, "The Necromancer of Dol Guldur." Mirkwood might still be known as Greenwood in The Rings of Power, but Dol Guldur has already made an appearance, though it is not yet Sauron's stronghold.

Sources indicate that the events in the Third Age occur long after the current Rings of Power storyline, suggesting that there may be a significant time jump, or the story will end before the Third Age begins, potentially leaving room for more of the story to be told through a different series. This could take the franchise into true horror territory, with Sauron channeling necromancy and corrupting his surroundings. The exact timeline for The Rings of Power has not yet been revealed, but with two more seasons to go, this was the turning point where the blacksmith became the necromancer.

Set in the Second Age of Middle-earth, The Rings of Power explores the forging of the iconic rings, the rise of the Dark Lord Sauron, and the epic events leading up to the stories in J.R.R. Tolkien's classic novels.

12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

In a recent development, as for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting latest movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

Go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

According to recent reports, pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Industry observers note that get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should plan ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you plan to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

The most important advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests.
  • Industry observers note that if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

Industry observers note that if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Industry observers note that hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

In a recent development, if you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

When you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

While driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

Sources indicate that when you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.
